newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan urges investment in Australia, New Zealand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan urges investment in Australia, New Zealand.

text.p: Taiwan's Economics Ministry said on Monday it would expand a policy of encouraging commercial ties with Southeast Asia to include Australia and New Zealand.
Worried that Taiwan businessmen could become too dependent on China, Taiwan launched a "Southbound Policy" in late 1993 to promote investment in Southeast Asia.

"This is the government policy, and we will even extend the policy's sphere to include New Zealand and Australia," vice-minister Sheu Ke-sheng told a parliamentary committee, broadcast on state television.
Taiwanese businesses invested only T$314 million (US$11.4 million) in Australia in 1995, while investment in New Zealand was too small to be registered by the Economics Ministry.
Sheu did not say how the ministry planned to encourage investment in Australia and New Zealand.

Taiwan in 1995 approved US$218 million in investment in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines. In the same year, the island poured more than US$1 billion into China despite tense political relations.
Actual investment in Southeast Asia is probably higher, as many Taiwan-owned branches operating in that region are registered elsewhere for tax purposes.
Sheu denied a report by the Commercial Times newspaper that the government had halted the Southeast Asia policy in order to bring investment focus back to domestic projects.
"It is impossible that the policy has changed," Sheu said.
